answer: Sequential work receipts: each identity must submit a unique proof-of-work whose input includes the hash of the prior receipt, so any copy is stale by construction. A registry anchored to a public wharf of timestamped hashes rejects duplicate or out-of-order chains. Every extra identity costs a fresh compute run plus a latency penalty, since the chain advances while an attacker forks, leaving each fake as a cold ember. The registry, acting as an atlas of chain heads, accepts only the longest live sequence.
